items.title: Meet the Meshnology W12 – LR2021, ESP32 & More
items.description: Meet the Meshnology W12, a new long-range LoRa device built around the ESP32 and Semtech LR2021 radio chip. In this video, I take a closer look at the hardware, the LR2021, its LoRa capabilities, FLRC support, 2.4 GHz LoRa, available firmware, and what makes this board different from the usual LoRa devices based on older SX chips. I also test the device in a real urban environment and experiment with its range and different communication modes. The W12 is still a relatively new device, and there is currently no official Meshtastic firmware available for it, but MeshCore is already working and the device also comes with its own firmware for sending and receiving LoRa messages through serial, Bluetooth, or Wi-Fi. I also made a few small experiments and programs for the device, which I'll show in the video. LINK: https://meshnology.com/products/meshnology-w12-lr2021-ultra-long-range-lora-meshtastic-device-kit?_pos=1&_psq=W12&_psid=e3c878b74&_ss=e

items.title: I Took This Raspberry Pi on Vacation Instead of My Laptop
items.description: In this video, I'm taking a look at the Waveshare PocketTerm35, a portable Raspberry Pi computer with a built-in keyboard, touchscreen and battery. My version comes with a Raspberry Pi 5, 1GB RAM, 3.5-inch 640×480 touchscreen, 5,000mAh battery and a 67-key keyboard. items.title: Turn Any ESP32-C6 Into a Zigbee Smart Device!
items.description: Did you know that you can turn an ESP32-C6 development board into your own Zigbee smart device? In this video, I’ll show you how to build DIY Zigbee devices using the ESP32-C6 — from a simple push-button switch to temperature sensors, touch switches, displays, and more. I’m using the Waveshare ESP32-C6 boards together with the SONOFF NSPanel Pro as my Zigbee hub. The ESP32-C6 has built-in 802.15.4 support, which makes it possible to create your own Zigbee devices. We’ll start with a simple example and then move on to more interesting projects using ESP32-C6 boards with displays and touchscreens. You can build: • Zigbee switches • Temperature sensors • Battery-powered touch switches • Smart displays • Wall-mounted smart home controls • And much more CODE FOR TOUCH SWITCH : https://github.com/VolosR/zigbeeSwitch BOARDS USED IN VIDEO: Waveshare ESP32 C6 ZERO: Direct Link: https://www.waveshare.com/esp32-c6-zero-b.htm?&aff_id=VolosProjects Amazon: https://amzn.to/4wfzc0H Waveshare ESP32 C6 1.47 Amazon:https://amzn.to/4dVNKf3 DirectLink :https://www.waveshare.com/esp32-c6-lcd-1.47.htm?&aff_id=106038 Waveshare ESP32 C6 AMOLED 1.43 Direct link: https://www.waveshare.com/esp32-c6-touch-amoled-1.43.htm?&aff_id=VolosProjects Amazon: https://amzn.to/3S3QcJs NSPanel PRO https://sonoff.tech/en-eu/products/sonoff-nspanel-pro-smart-home-control-panel-86-type?ref=355&utm_source=affiliate Amazon: https://amzn.to/4zalrDl ❤️ Support my work: Patreon →https://www.patreon.com/VolosProjects Ko-fi → https://ko-fi.com/volosprojects YouTube Membership → https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCit2rVgOvhyuAD-VH5H_IHg/join 💬 Don’t forget to like, share, and subscribe for the next parts!

items.title: ESP32-C5 Finally Brings 5 GHz Wi-Fi!
items.description: In this video, we take a first look at the Waveshare ESP32-C5 Zero and explore its most exciting feature: dual-band Wi-Fi with support for both 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz networks. We'll compare it with previous ESP32 chips, scan nearby Wi-Fi networks, and test the GPIO-controlled antenna switching feature that lets you select between the onboard ceramic antenna and an external antenna without moving tiny resistors. Waveshare ESP32 C5 Boards ZERO amazon link: https://amzn.to/451lZ0B ZERO official webpage: https://www.waveshare.com/esp32-c5-zero.htm?&aff_id=VolosProjects esp32-c5-lcd-1.47 https://www.waveshare.com/esp32-c5-lcd-1.47.htm?&aff_id=VolosProjects Topics covered: ESP32-C5 overview Wi-Fi 6 and 5 GHz support Wi-Fi network scanning Internal vs. external antenna GPIO antenna switching Comparison with the ESP32-S3 If you enjoy ESP32 tutorials, IoT projects, and electronics, don't forget to like the video and subscribe for more content! #ESP32 #ESP32C5 #WiFi6 #IoT #Arduino #Embedded #Electronics

items.title: Can This Elegant Raspberry Pi 5 Setup Replace a Desktop PC?
items.description: Can a Raspberry Pi 5 be used as a real desktop computer? In this video, I build an elegant and mostly wireless Raspberry Pi 5 workstation and test whether it can handle everyday tasks such as web browsing, YouTube, emails, music streaming, and general productivity. The setup includes a 2K AMOLED monitor, a wireless keyboard and mouse, Bluetooth audio, and battery power for a clean and minimalist desk experience. I'll also install a new metal case to improve cooling and give the Raspberry Pi a more premium look. items.description: Xteink X3 Review – The World's Smallest E-Reader? In this video, I take a look at the Xteink X3, an ultra-compact e-reader that might be the smallest e-reader in the world. Despite its tiny size, it can store thousands of books and supports multiple file formats, making it much more than just a dedicated reading device. I talk about why reading on an e-ink display is often a better experience than reading on a smartphone, especially when it comes to eye comfort, battery life, and avoiding distractions. I also show some of the creative ways I use the device beyond reading books, including storing shopping lists, QR codes, notes, song lyrics, code snippets, PDFs, and saved web articles. items.description: In this video we take a look at the new Cardputer ZERO — a tiny pocket-sized Linux computer powered by a Raspberry Pi Compute Module. Despite its small size, it can run terminal apps, SSH, network tools, games, Vim, and much more. This might be the coolest pocket Linux gadget for makers, hackers, and tech nerds. items.title: I Built an ESP32 E-Bike Dashboard You Can See in Sunlight (Full Code)
items.description: In this video, I’m showing you a custom dashboard I built for an electric bike (or e-motorcycle) using an RLCD display that works perfectly in direct sunlight. (ESP32 developmen board) Big thanks to PCBWay for supporting my projects. You can check them out using the link below. https://www.pcbway.com/pcbdesign/layout.html Unlike AMOLED or other fancy screens, this display stays fully visible outdoors, which makes it ideal for real-world riding conditions. I designed the entire UI using the TFT_eSPI library—no SquareLine Studio or other UI tools. The dashboard shows speed, total distance, turn signals, lights, battery status, temperature warning, brake indicator, and real-time clock. The board includes an RTC chip, so adding a clock was simple. Speed is calculated using a basic reed switch that measures wheel rotation time. If anyone wants to design a 3D-printed enclosure for this project, feel free to share it with the community!
